Permanganate ($\text{MnO}_4^-$) contains manganese in the $+7$ oxidation state. Manganese is a group 7 element with a ground-state electron configuration of $[\text{Ar}]3\text{d}^5 4\text{s}^2$. Therefore, $\text{Mn}^{7+}$ has a $\text{d}^0$ electron configuration.

Ligand-field analysis using Tanabe-Sugano diagrams or Racah parameters ($B$ and $C$) is used to describe electronic transitions between different terms arising from the splitting of the $\text{d}$-orbitals in the presence of ligands (d-d transitions). Because the $\text{Mn}^{7+}$ ion has no $\text{d}$ electrons, d-d transitions are impossible.

The observed absorption bands at $17,570$, $31,560$, and $38,320\text{ cm}^{-1}$ are very intense ($\epsilon \approx 1,500\text{--}3,000\text{ M}^{-1}\text{cm}^{-1}$), which is characteristic of spin-allowed and Laporte-allowed transitions. These are **Ligand-to-Metal Charge Transfer (LMCT)** transitions, where electrons move from the $\text{O}^{2-}$ ligands to the empty $\text{d}$-orbitals of the $\text{Mn}^{7+}$ center.

Since these are not d-d transitions, the ligand-field splitting parameter $Dq$ and the Racah parameter $B$ cannot be determined from this spectrum using the standard ligand-field model.
